newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria banks to cut interest rates on loans in 97.
newsitem.headline: Algeria banks to cut interest rates on loans in 97.

text.p: Algerian commercial banks will cut loan interest rates to between 15 and 19.5 percent next year against 18.5 and 23.5 percent in 1996, officials and Algeria's official news agency APS said on Monday.

"Interest rates on loans granted by commercial banks will be reduced from January 1, 1997, to between 15 and 19.5 percent," APS said, quoting the Algerian Association of Banks and Financial Institutions.
Current interest rates are set at a ceiling of 18.5 percent for short term loans (52 weeks) and 23.5 percent for long-term loans (10 years), APS said.

"With the support of the public authorities, the new measure (interest rate cut) was taken after a clean up of the commercial banks provisions...And since half a year, the banks have set up a plan of action to upgrade the country's industrial enterprises, including rescheduling their debt," APS said.
A spokesman at the central bank (Banque d'Algerie) told Reuters by telephone: "The commercial banks' move follows the central bank recent decision to cut the discount rate."
Last August, Banque d'Algerie lowered the discount rate 1.0 percent to 13 percent to spur economic growth and improve the financing conditions of the enterprises, officials had said.
Officials at the association were not immediately available for comment.
